newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Omani firm signs $43 mln Tanzania hydro project.
newsitem.headline: Omani firm signs $43 mln Tanzania hydro project.

text.p: An Omani company, Rawahy Enterprises, has signed a preliminary agreement on a $43 million deal to build a hydro-electric dam in Tanzania, a senior company official said on Friday.
Rawahy construction manager Jang Bahadur Singh said a memorandum of understanding was signed after negotiations at an international investor forum in Tanzania.
Singh said the deal, believed to be the biggest single contract signed during the four-day forum, was a joint venture with Tanzania's state-run electricity body, Tanesco.
The build operate and transfer (BOT) project is proposed for northern Mandera region and provides for building a hydro-electric dam of 21 megawatt capacity.

"We have signed the deal on the hydropower plant as a memorandum of understanding. This will be our first project in Tanzania," Singh told Reuters, adding his company had negotiated for two other projects worth more than $100 million.

Singh said the company expected to open a representative office in Tanzania within two months. "It's a memorandum of understanding which we regard as a preliminary understanding necessary for finalising details of a contract, but there is no reason to pull out."

The two other projects Rawahy was bidding for are a $5 million hotel on the Indian Ocean island of Zanzibar and a 25 percent share in a $400 million BOT project to build an underground petroleum pipeline.

"For the $5 million hotel project at Zanzibar, we hope to finalise the paperwork within a couple of months. For the petroleum pipeline from Dar es Salaam to (northwestern) Mwanza we are very much interested in being part of that."
Rawahy Enterprises, the only forum entrant from Oman, gave its annual turnover in 1995 as $15 million.
